Absolutely! This phenomenon is a great example of cognitive dissonance, a psychological concept where people hold two or more conflicting beliefs, ideas, or values at the same time, which causes mental discomfort. To reduce this discomfort, they might change one of their beliefs or justify their actions, even if it goes against facts.

In this case, followers may justify the TikTok creator's copyright infringement because admitting wrongdoing by their favorite influencer would create cognitive dissonance. By supporting the creator and justifying their actions, followers maintain a positive image of their idol and reduce the mental discomfort caused by cognitive dissonance.

It's also important to note that strong emotional attachments, like those formed with popular idols, can lead people to disregard facts and make irrational decisions. This emotional bond can create a powerful motivation for people to defend and support their favorite figures, even in the face of conflicting evidence.
